member.name: T:NinePatchWpf.NinePatchZoomViewer
member.summary:
A zoomable, scrollable view of many nine-patches, with DAW-style s: drag a thumb to scroll, drag a thumb edge to zoom that axis.
CONTENT is a list of s in world units (for a piano roll: X = ticks, Y = note row). × is the world size. The visible part is rendered with one native call into a bitmap of the viewport's size in device pixels, so the cost depends on what is visible, not on the zoom or the content size.
VIEW: / are DIPs per world unit, / the world coordinates at the top-left corner. The thumbs always show exactly that view: thumb length = visible world / content size, so zooming out to the whole content fills the track.
MOUSE over the content: wheel = scroll vertically, Shift+wheel = scroll horizontally, Ctrl+wheel = zoom horizontally around the mouse, Ctrl+Shift+wheel = zoom vertically, middle-drag = pan.
EXTRAS: and (rulers, piano keys) sit beside the view, on top of it (playhead, selection), and lets you draw grid lines underneath the elements. All of them follow the view through .

member.name: T:NinePatchWpf.ZoomScrollBar
member.summary:
DAW-style scroll bar whose thumb is also the zoom control.
The bar shows the visible part of the content as a fraction: the thumb starts at and is long (both 0–1 of the content).
MOUSE: drag the thumb body = scroll drag a thumb edge = zoom; the opposite edge stays put (Ctrl: both edges move, zoom around the centre) click / hold on the track = page towards the mouse double-click the thumb = show everything; again = back to the previous view wheel = scroll; Ctrl+wheel = zoom around the thumb centre
When the thumb would be shorter than it is drawn at that size, and dragging its edges zooms exponentially, so you can keep zooming in with a thumb that stays grabbable.
The bar is drawn with vector shapes from the brush properties. Set and (and optionally , ) to skin it with nine-patches instead; the edge grips are drawn on top either way.

member.name: T:NinePatchWpf.NinePatchSkinCache
member.summary:
Shared cache of nine-patch source images and rendered bitmaps.
Every NinePatch control draws through a cache: the one set with (inherited down the tree), else , else . The cache owns the source images, so controls never load or dispose them themselves.
Rendered bitmaps are frozen, shared between controls that draw the same skin at the same pixel size and DPI, and evicted least-recently-used once either or is exceeded. All members are thread-safe.
